checked: Forty-seven of the fifty issues of Seconds dated 2002 to 2008 were pulled and are now at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_sga-seconds-2002-2008/, 26 MB, named by their own date. Three could not be had: nl20 of 24 April 2007 and nl60 of 5 February 2008 have no Wayback snapshot of the file on either URL form or timestamp, and nl55 of 23 October 2007 has no download link on its record page at all. Every issue has a clean embedded text layer. METHOD: each page was tested two ways at once - matched by name against all 126 people on this block, and rendered grey at 100 dpi and block-scanned for halftone regions in the body of the page, with the black masthead band and the grey sidebar excluded. Only six pages carry both a name from this block and a picture-shaped region, and all six were rendered and read.
why: Not one member of this block is photographed in SGA's own newsletter. Every picture-shaped region on those six pages is clip art: a trophy for the Senator Spotlight box, a piggy bank, balloons, a smiley, Captain Planet, a turkey, a leprechaun. The Spotlight, which names a member every week and looked like the best chance on this block, is illustrated with the same trophy every time. The photographs that do appear are of the executive - a face beside Jeanne Johnson on 17 October 2006 and one captioned as Ashley Gore on the same page - and both already have portraits. WHAT THE FILE IS STILL WORTH: it is SGA's own week-by-week record of the autumn 2006 semester, which no Herald covers, it prints the bill and resolution numbers, and it names the whole intake in its welcome lists - eighteen new senators on 27 September 2005 and the whole 2007-08 intake on 25 September 2007. Anyone writing up 2006-07 should read it.

kind: method and coverage: the bulk harvest the brief asked for, and what it returned
name: Labelled-frame harvest of the 2002-2009 Herald, run backwards from the index to the names
checked: The two earlier passes on this block searched NAME to INDEX. This one ran INDEX to NAME, which is a different question and catches labels the earlier direction cannot: a corrupted spelling, a nickname, a reversed order. FOUR HARVESTS. (1) Every text line in all 375 staged Herald PDFs 2002-2009 was read through the embedded text layer with geometry, and every line that is nothing but a personal name of two to four capitalised words was kept with its bounding box, its type height, and the text directly above and below it: 65,839 label lines, 18,084 distinct strings. Matched against the 126 with an exact surname and a given name allowed to vary through a nickname table or a true initial, it gave 207 hits on 45 people, 196 after de-duplicating the two issues that are staged twice. (2) Every one of those 196 was ink-probed on the page image - strips 0.005 of page height deep up and down the label's own column at 110 dpi, dark-pixel fraction, longest run at or above 0.40 - and every candidate with a run of two strips or more that was not already written up in these notes was rendered and read by eye. (3) The 2007-2009 caption index was harvested for mugshot-shaped frames, meaning an embedded image under 320 points square carrying a bare personal name above, below or beside it: 663 frames, 253 distinct label strings, and NOT ONE of the 126 is among them. (4) The People Poll's label geometry - a bare name with a home-town-and-class line directly beneath - was applied to 2006-2009 for the first time, which the 1993-2005 bulk sweep never covered: 702 such labels, six matching this block.
why: The whole harvest yielded no publishable Herald portrait, and that is now a measured result rather than an impression. Everything the ink probe raised turned out to be a chapter advertisement, a printed list, a headline or a pull quote: the Alpha Delta Pi Crush Dance list of 5 December 2002, the Kappa Delta council advertisement of 21 November 2002, the Alpha Omicron Pi new members of 9 September 2004, the Chi Omega new members of 21 September 2004, the Dynamic Leadership Institute members of 28 April 2005, the Sigma Kappa new members of 28 August 2007. The four new poll-shaped hits are the same: Zack Rockrohr of 17 November 2009 p4B is a pull quote in a Weezer story with no frame anywhere near it, and the dark ink the probe found beneath it is a Papa John's advertisement. The Herald of 2002-2009 is now worked from both directions and should be treated as closed for these 126 people.

kind: identification check made and exhausted, for the editor deciding the Cortney entry
name: Keanan Noel Cortney: the spelling cannot be settled from SGA's side
checked: TopSCHOLAR files fifty-four sets of SGA minutes for 2002-03. Ten spread across the whole year were pulled and their text read - 21 October, 5 November, 2 December 1902 [2002], 21 and 29 October, 12 November, 29 January, 11 and 25 February, 11 March and 8 April - and the name Cortney, Courtney or Keanan appears in none of them. The minutes of 1 October 2002 were rendered at six times scale and the printed line read by eye: 'Keanan Noel Cortney-At large rep', one of three sworn in that evening beside Kelly Johnson and John Law. That is the archive's only source for her and the only SGA record of the name.
why: So the two spellings cannot be reconciled from within SGA's own papers, and the editor is deciding between a typed minute that says Cortney and a Vantine Studios composite plate and a Phi Mu new-member advertisement that both say Courtney. Everything else lines up: the composite is the 2002-2003 plate, the advertisement ran on 12 September 2002 and the swearing-in was on 1 October, and the given name Keanan occurs exactly once in 5,623 digitised Herald pages. The portrait is cut and filed and the entry carries the reasoning; nothing further can be established without a source outside SGA and the Herald.
